items.title: 9 midcap stocks with over 50% YoY sales growth
items.description: A significant rise in quarterly sales on a year-over-year (YoY) basis indicates growth in a company’s revenue during the period. Among the NSE Midcap segment, excluding banking and financial stocks, nine companies recorded sales growth of more than 50% in the June 2026 quarter compared with the same period in 2025, according to turnover scan data from StockEdge.com.

items.title: Will Nifty, Sensex tumble on Monday? 5 factors which will drive D-Street action this week
items.description: Following a 7-week decline in Nifty, Dalal Street faces a holiday-shortened week driven by five key factors: escalating US-Iran conflict, Brent crude trading above $104, US 10-year Treasury yields above 5.1%, continued FII outflows, and rupee volatility within the 95.50-96.50 trading band.

items.title: 11 penny stocks surged up to 110% in just 3 months. 3 turned multibaggers
items.description: Over the last three months, 11 penny stocks delivered returns ranging from 30% to 110%. These stocks were identified using a defined set of filters: a market capitalisation of less than Rs 1,000 crore, a share price below Rs 20, and a minimum latest trading volume of 5 lakh shares. The screening criteria were used to identify low-priced, actively traded micro-cap stocks that had delivered strong upward price momentum. (Data Source: ACE Equity)

items.title: Bonus & dividends: SAIL, IGL among 10 stocks turning ex-record date this week. Do you own any?
items.description: Around 10 companies have set record dates for dividends and bonus issues between September 28 and October 1, making it a relatively quiet week for corporate actions. The market will remain closed on October 2 for Gandhi Jayanti, with BSE and NSE also shut on October 20 for Dussehra.

items.title: The most uncertain sector also pays the most to wait. Watchlist for patient investors: 5 stocks with upside potential of up to 25%
items.description: There are some interesting contrarian bets in the market. But going contrarian, or buying what everyone else is running away from, is not to be done casually. Done wrong, it is just recklessness. It becomes a sensible move only when there is a solid, logical reason behind it. So, the real question is not whether some companies are beaten down. The question is whether there is a good reason to buy them anyway.
